key_insight: Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization (GGPO) removes learner-to-behavior importance weights by optimizing a KL-adjusted log-mean-exp gap over grouped responses, yielding stable off-policy learning for verifiable-reward RL.
engineering_relevance: The method is directly useful for training large language models from stale or offline data, where reducing variance and handling policy mismatch are critical for scalable deployment.
method: Optimize a contrast of KL-adjusted rewards within response groups for the same prompt.
Derive the objective from KL-regularized policy optimization, linking it to the optimality gap on-policy.
Use reference refresh to track Gibbs-target composition and control policy staleness.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, GGPO outperforms GRPO and AGRO under training-inference mismatch and on fixed offline data, with a reported five-benchmark average of 46.58 using the default refresh schedule versus 32.96 with a fixed reference.
watch_item: Performance depends on reference refresh and coverage assumptions, so stale references or poor support over responses may weaken the theoretical and empirical gains.
paper_title: Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards
